pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded items are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test/done.test.js 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only the open items in id order.
test/done.test.js 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and checks the order and the ✓ prefix.
test/done.test.js 'AC-4' checks all items, in order, with ✓ on the done one.
test/done.test.js 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for each view and for /.
test/done.test.js 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values; the code uses Object.hasOwn.
test/done.test.js 'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in all three views.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all, but no test names AC-8 or reads routes.json. Removing the routes would break no test. The spec does not mark the item 'verified by review'.

findings.what: No test proves AC-8. Nothing asserts that traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all. The only route-related tests cover the checker's regex, with a made-up route list.
findings.fix: Add an 'AC-8' test that reads traffic/routes.json and expects it to include '/?view=done' and '/?view=all'. Preferably also request each route against the app and expect a 2xx.

findings.what: The traffic checker's regex change goes beyond the spec. The PR discloses it, and it is needed for the new routes.
findings.fix: None needed; the disclosure is sufficient.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. Both decisions are followed: the default view is open, and the view is a query parameter.
AC-1 to AC-7 are met and tested. AC-8 has no test. All six state-table rows have tests.

Tests for AC-1 to AC-7 and the states would fail if the code were wrong. AC-8 is untested. I did not run the suite here; CI runs it. The follow-up commit only deleted 4 blank lines from test/done.test.js.
README describes the views. The CLAUDE.md rule about adding routes to routes.json is followed.
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup. The SQL fragments come from a fixed table, not from user input. The empty-table check is correct.
The view value is whitelisted. Output is HTML-escaped. No secrets or planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with a nav line; no UI files (CSS, components) are in the diff.
No browser flow was available. The list page is server-rendered HTML and is covered by the worker tests.
The claims match the diff. The PR says test/traffic.test.js now records the query string, and it does. The title is under 72 characters.
